sanskrit: karṇas tv eko yudhāṃ śreṣṭho vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ dahañ śatrūn naravyāghra śuśubhe sa paraṃtapaḥ
english: But Karṇa alone, foremost of warriors, blazed forth like a smokeless fire; burning up his foes, O tiger among men, that scorcher of enemies shone resplendent.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ karṇena pāñcālāś cedibhiḥ saha tatra tatra vyamuhyanta vanadāhe yathā dvipāḥ cukruśus te naravyāghra yathāprāg vā narottamāḥ
english: Slaughtered by Karṇa, the Pāñcālas together with the Cedis reeled this way and that, bewildered like elephants caught in a forest fire; and they cried out, O tiger among men, those best of men, as they had done before.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu krośatāṃ śrutvā bhītānāṃ raṇamūrdhani dhāvatāṃ ca diśo rājan vitrastānāṃ samantataḥ ārtanādo mahāṃs tatra pretānām iva saṃplave
english: Hearing them cry out, terrified at the head of the battle, fleeing in all directions, O king, panic-stricken on every side, there arose a great wail of anguish, like that of the dead at the dissolution of the world.

sanskrit: vadhyamānāṃs tu tān dṛṣṭvā sūtaputreṇa māriṣa vitresuḥ sarvabhūtāni tiryagyonigatāny api
english: Seeing them being slain by the Sūta's son, O venerable one, all creatures trembled, even those born in the brute creation.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare sūtaputreṇa sṛñjayāḥ arjunaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca vyākrośanta muhur muhuḥ pretarājapure yadvat pretarājaṃ vicetasaḥ
english: Cut down in battle by the Sūta's son, the Sṛñjayas called out again and again upon Arjuna and Vāsudeva, as the senseless dead cry out upon the King of the Dead in his own city.

sanskrit: athābravīd vāsudevaṃ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ bhārgavāstraṃ mahāghoraṃ dṛṣṭvā tatra sabhīritam
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya, son of Kuntī, spoke to Vāsudeva, seeing the most terrible Bhārgava weapon loosed there with fury:

sanskrit: paśya kṛṣṇa mahābāho bhārgavāstrasya vikramam naitad astraṃ hi samare śakyaṃ hantuṃ kathaṃ cana
english: "Behold, mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, the prowess of the Bhārgava weapon! This weapon can in no way be countered in battle.

sanskrit: sūtaputraṃ ca saṃrabdhaṃ paśya kṛṣṇa mahāraṇe antakapratimaṃ vīraṃ kurvāṇaṃ karma dāruṇam
english: And behold the Sūta's son in his fury, O Kṛṣṇa, in this great battle—a hero like Death himself, working a fearful slaughter.

sanskrit: sutīkṣṇaṃ codayann aśvān prekṣate māṃ muhur muhuḥ na ca paśyāmi samare karṇasya prapalāyitam
english: Sharply urging on his horses, he looks toward me again and again; nor do I see any sign that Karṇa would flee from the field.

sanskrit: jīvan prāpnoti puruṣaḥ saṃkhye jayaparājayau jitasya tu hṛṣīkeśa vadha eva kuto jayaḥ
english: A man who lives wins in battle either victory or defeat; but for one already conquered, O Hṛṣīkeśa, there is only death—how then can there be victory?"

sanskrit: tato janārdanaḥ prāyād draṣṭum icchan yudhiṣṭhiram śrameṇa grāhayiṣyaṃś ca karṇaṃ yuddhena māriṣa
english: Then Janārdana set off, wishing to see Yudhiṣṭhira, and resolved to wear Karṇa down by exertion in the fight, O venerable one.

sanskrit: arjunaṃ cābravīt kṛṣṇo bhṛśaṃ rājā parikṣataḥ tam āśvāsya kuruśreṣṭha tataḥ karṇaṃ haniṣyasi
english: And Kṛṣṇa said to Arjuna: "The king is sorely wounded. Comfort him first, O best of the Kurus, and then you shall slay Karṇa."

sanskrit: tato dhanaṃjayo draṣṭuṃ rājānaṃ bāṇapīḍitam rathena prayayau kṣipraṃ saṃgrāme keśavājñayā
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya, to see the king tormented by arrows, drove swiftly upon his chariot through the battle at Keśava's command.

sanskrit: gacchann eva tu kaunteyo dharmarājadidṛkṣayā sainyam ālokayām āsa nāpaśyat tatra cāgrajam
english: As the son of Kuntī went on, wishing to behold the King of Righteousness, he scanned the host but did not see his elder brother there.

sanskrit: yuddhaṃ kṛtvā tu kaunteyo droṇaputreṇa bhārata duḥsahaṃ vajriṇā saṃkhye parājigye bhṛgoḥ sutam
english: Having waged an unbearable combat with Droṇa's son, O Bhārata, the wielder of the thunderbolt-like bow, the son of Kuntī overcame in battle the descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: drauṇiṃ parājitya tatogradhanvā; kṛtvā mahad duṣkaram āryakarma ālokayām āsa tataḥ svasainyaṃ; dhanaṃjayaḥ śatrubhir apradhṛṣyaḥ
english: Having vanquished Droṇa's son, that fierce bowman, having accomplished a great and arduous deed of nobility, Dhanaṃjaya then surveyed his own army—he whom no enemies could assail.

sanskrit: sa yudhyamānaḥ pṛtanāmukhasthāñ; śūrāñ śūro harṣayan savyasācī pūrvāpadānaiḥ prathitaiḥ praśaṃsan; sthirāṃś cakārātmarathān anīke
english: As he fought, that hero Savyasācin cheered the brave men stationed at the front of the host; praising them with renowned deeds of old, he made firm in the line the warriors of his own chariot-division.

sanskrit: apaśyamānas tu kirīṭamālī; yudhi jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaram ājamīḍham uvāca bhīmaṃ tarasābhyupetya; rājñaḥ pravṛttis tv iha keti rājan
english: But the diademed, garlanded one, not seeing in the fight his eldest brother, scion of Ajamīḍha, approached Bhīma swiftly and said, "What news is there here, O king, of the king?"

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca apayāta ito rājā dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ karṇabāṇavibhugnāṅgo yadi jīvet kathaṃ cana
english: Bhīma said: "The king, Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Dharma, has withdrawn from here, his limbs broken by Karṇa's arrows—if indeed he yet lives at all."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca tasmād bhavāñ śīghram itaḥ prayātu; rājñaḥ pravṛttyai kurusattamasya nūnaṃ hi viddho 'tibhṛśaṃ pṛṣatkaiḥ; karṇena rājā śibiraṃ gato 'sau
english: Arjuna said: "Then go you swiftly from here for news of the king, best of the Kurus; for surely, pierced most grievously by Karṇa's shafts, the king has gone to the camp."

sanskrit: yaḥ saṃprahāre niśi saṃpravṛtte; droṇena viddho 'tibhṛśaṃ tarasvī tasthau ca tatrāpi jayapratīkṣo; droṇena yāvan na hataḥ kilāsīt
english: "He who, in the night battle when it was joined, though pierced most grievously by Droṇa, that impetuous one stood his ground even there, awaiting victory, so long as he was not slain by Droṇa—

sanskrit: sa saṃśayaṃ gamitaḥ pāṇḍavāgryaḥ; saṃkhye 'dya karṇena mahānubhāvaḥ jñātuṃ prayāhy āśu tam adya bhīma; sthāsyāmy ahaṃ śatrugaṇān nirudhya
english: that foremost of the Pāṇḍavas, that great-souled one, has today been brought into peril by Karṇa in battle. Go quickly now to learn of him, O Bhīma; I shall stand here, holding back the enemy hosts."

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca tvam eva jānīhi mahānubhāva; rājñaḥ pravṛttiṃ bharatarṣabhasya ahaṃ hi yady arjuna yāmi tatra; vakṣyanti māṃ bhīta iti pravīrāḥ
english: Bhīma said: "Go you yourself, great-souled one, to learn the news of the king, that bull of the Bhāratas; for if I go there, Arjuna, the warriors will say of me, 'He is afraid.'"

sanskrit: tato 'bravīd arjuno bhīmasenaṃ; saṃśaptakāḥ pratyanīkaṃ sthitā me etān ahatvā na mayā tu śakyam; ito 'payātuṃ ripusaṃghagoṣṭhāt
english: Then Arjuna said to Bhīmasena: "The sworn warriors stand arrayed against me; without slaying these, I cannot withdraw from here, from this throng of the enemy host."

sanskrit: athābravīd arjunaṃ bhīmasenaḥ; svavīryam āśritya kurupravīra saṃśaptakān pratiyotsyāmi saṃkhye; sarvān ahaṃ yāhi dhanaṃjayeti
english: Then Bhīmasena said to Arjuna: "Relying on my own valor, O foremost of the Kurus, I shall fight back against all the sworn warriors in battle—go, Dhanaṃjaya!"

sanskrit: tad bhīmasenasya vaco niśamya; sudurvacaṃ bhrātur amitramadhye draṣṭuṃ kuruśreṣṭham abhiprayātuṃ; provāca vṛṣṇipravaraṃ tadānīm
english: Hearing these words of Bhīmasena, his brother, words most hard to utter in the midst of foes, Arjuna, resolving to go and behold the best of the Kurus, then spoke to the foremost of the Vṛṣṇis:

sanskrit: codayāśvān hṛṣīkeśa vigāhyaitaṃ rathārṇavam ajātaśatruṃ rājānaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi keśava
english: "Urge on the horses, Hṛṣīkeśa, and plunge through this ocean of chariots; I wish to behold King Ajātaśatru, O Keśava."

sanskrit: tato hayān sarvadāśārhamukhyaḥ; prācodayad bhīmam uvāca cedam naitac citraṃ tava karmādya vīra; yāsyāmahe jahi bhīmārisaṃghān
english: Then the chief of all the Dāśārhas urged on the horses and said this to Bhīma: "This deed of yours today is no wonder, O hero; we shall go—slay the enemy hosts, Bhīma."

sanskrit: tato yayau hṛṣīkeśo yatra rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ śīghrāc chīghrataraṃ rājan vājibhir garuḍopamaiḥ
english: Then Hṛṣīkeśa drove on to where King Yudhiṣṭhira was, faster and faster, O king, with steeds that rivaled Garuḍa.

sanskrit: pratyanīke vyavasthāpya bhīmasenam ariṃdamam saṃdiśya caiva rājendra yuddhaṃ prati vṛkodaram
english: Having stationed Bhīmasena, that subduer of foes, against the opposing line, and having given Vṛkodara his charge concerning the battle, O lord of kings—

sanskrit: tatas tu gatvā puruṣapravīrau; rājānam āsādya śayānam ekam rathād ubhau pratyavaruhya tasmād; vavandatur dharmarājasya pādau
english: then those two foremost of men, having gone and come upon the king lying alone, both descended from the chariot and bowed at the feet of the King of Righteousness.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā puruṣavyāghrau kṣemiṇau puruṣarṣabha mudābhyupagatau kṛṣṇāv aśvināv iva vāsavam
english: Beholding those two tigers among men come to him unharmed and in joy, O bull among men—the two Kṛṣṇas, like the Aśvins approaching Vāsava—

sanskrit: tāv abhyanandad rājā hi vivasvān aśvināv iva hate mahāsure jambhe śakraviṣṇū yathā guruḥ
english: the king welcomed them, as Vivasvat welcomes the Aśvins, or as the preceptor welcomed Śakra and Viṣṇu when the great Asura Jambha had been slain.

sanskrit: manyamāno hataṃ karṇaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ harṣagadgadayā vācā prītaḥ prāha paraṃtapau
english: Believing Karṇa slain, Yudhiṣṭhira, the King of Righteousness, well pleased, addressed those two scorchers of foes in a voice faltering with joy.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca mahāsattvau tu tau dṛṣṭvā sahitau keśavārjunau hatam ādhirathiṃ mene saṃkhye gāṇḍīvadhanvanā
english: Saṃjaya said: But seeing those two of great spirit, Keśava and Arjuna, come together, he supposed the son of Adhiratha had been slain in battle by the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: tāv abhyanandat kaunteyaḥ sāmnā paramavalgunā smitapūrvam amitraghnaḥ pūjayan bharatarṣabha
english: The son of Kuntī welcomed them with words most gracious and kind, that slayer of foes honoring them with a smile, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca svāgataṃ devakīputra svāgataṃ te dhanaṃjaya priyaṃ me darśanaṃ bāḍhaṃ yuvayor acyutārjunau
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Welcome, son of Devakī! Welcome to you, Dhanaṃjaya! Dear to me indeed is the sight of you both, O Acyuta and Arjuna.

sanskrit: akṣatābhyām ariṣṭābhyāṃ kathaṃ yudhya mahāratham āśīviṣasamaṃ yuddhe sarvaśastraviśāradam
english: Unhurt and unscathed, how did you fight that great chariot-warrior, like a venomous serpent in battle, skilled in every weapon—

sanskrit: agragaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ śarma varma ca rakṣitaṃ vṛṣasenena suṣeṇena ca dhanvinā
english: the foremost of all the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, their refuge and their armor, guarded by Vṛṣasena and by the archer Suṣeṇa—

sanskrit: anujñātaṃ mahāvīryaṃ rameṇāstreṣu durjayam trātāraṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ gantāraṃ vāhinīmukhe
english: of mighty valor, sanctioned by Rāma, invincible in arms, the protector of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who advanced at the head of the host—

sanskrit: hantāram arisainyānām amitragaṇamardanam duryodhanahite yuktam asmadyuddhāya codyatam
english: the destroyer of enemy armies, the crusher of hostile throngs, devoted to Duryodhana's welfare and ever ready for battle with us—

sanskrit: apradhṛṣyaṃ mahāyuddhe devair api savāsavaiḥ analānilayos tulyaṃ tejasā ca balena ca
english: unassailable in great battle even by the gods with Vāsava at their head, equal to fire and wind in splendor and in might—

sanskrit: pātālam iva gambhīraṃ suhṛdānandavardhanam antakābham amitrāṇāṃ karṇaṃ hatvā mahāhave diṣṭyā yuvām anuprāptau jitvāsuram ivāmarau
english: deep as the netherworld, the increaser of his friends' joy, like Death to his foes—having slain Karṇa in the great battle, by good fortune you two have come back, like the immortals after conquering an Asura!

sanskrit: tena yuddham adīnena mayā hy adyācyutārjunau kupitenāntakeneva prajāḥ sarvā jighāṃsatā
english: For today, O Acyuta and Arjuna, I joined battle with that undaunted one, who, like enraged Death bent on destroying all creatures—

sanskrit: tena ketuś ca me chinno hatau ca pārṣṇisārathī hatavāhaḥ kṛtaś cāsmi yuyudhānasya paśyataḥ
english: by him my banner was cut down, and my flank-charioteers were slain, and my horses too were killed, while Yuyudhāna looked on—

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnasya yamayor vīrasya ca śikhaṇḍinaḥ paśyatāṃ draupadeyānāṃ pāñcālānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: while Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the twins, the heroic Śikhaṇḍin, the sons of Draupadī, and all the Pāñcālas looked on.

sanskrit: etāñ jitvā mahāvīryān karṇaḥ śatrugaṇān bahūn jitavān māṃ mahābāho yatamānaṃ mahāraṇe
english: Having vanquished these mighty warriors and many enemy throngs, Karṇa overcame me too, O mighty-armed one, as I strove in the great battle.

sanskrit: anusṛtya ca māṃ yuddhe paruṣāṇy uktavān bahu tatra tatra yudhāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ paribhūya na saṃśayaḥ
english: And pursuing me in the fight, that foremost of warriors spoke many a harsh word, again and again, scorning me—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaprabhāvāt tu yaj jīvāmi dhanaṃjaya bahunātra kim uktena nāhaṃ tat soḍhum utsahe
english: That I live at all, Dhanaṃjaya, is by the might of Bhīmasena. But what need of many words here?—I have no will to endure that any longer.

sanskrit: trayodaśāhaṃ varṣāṇi yasmād bhīto dhanaṃjaya na sma nidrāṃ labhe rātrau na cāhani sukhaṃ kva cit
english: For thirteen years, Dhanaṃjaya, in fear of him I got no sleep by night, nor any ease by day at any time.

sanskrit: tasya dveṣeṇa saṃyuktaḥ paridahye dhanaṃjaya ātmano maraṇaṃ jānan vādhrīṇasa iva dvipaḥ
english: Seized with hatred of him, I am consumed within, Dhanaṃjaya, knowing my own death at hand, like an elephant who has scented the lion.

sanskrit: yasyāyam agamat kālaś cintayānasya me vibho kathaṃ śakyo mayā karṇo yuddhe kṣapayituṃ bhavet
english: All this time of mine has passed, O lord, in brooding upon this: how might Karṇa be destroyed by me in battle?

sanskrit: jāgrat svapaṃś ca kaunteya karṇam eva sadā hy aham paśyāmi tatra tatraiva karṇabhūtam idaṃ jagat
english: Waking and sleeping, son of Kuntī, ever I saw Karṇa and Karṇa alone; this whole world seemed to me to have become Karṇa, wherever I turned.

sanskrit: yatra yatra hi gacchāmi karṇād bhīto dhanaṃjaya tatra tatra hi paśyāmi karṇam evāgrataḥ sthitam
english: Wherever I went, Dhanaṃjaya, in dread of Karṇa, there too I would see Karṇa himself standing before me.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tenaiva vīreṇa samareṣv apalāyinā sahayaḥ sarathaḥ pārtha jitvā jīvan visarjitaḥ
english: And I, O Pārtha, conquered by that hero who never fled from battle, with my horses and my chariot, was spared alive and let go.

sanskrit: ko nu me jīvitenārtho rājyenārtho 'tha vā punaḥ mamaivaṃ dhikkṛtasyeha karṇenāhavaśobhinā
english: What use have I now of life, or what use again of a kingdom, thus disgraced as I am here by Karṇa, the ornament of battle?

sanskrit: na prāptapūrvaṃ yad bhīṣmāt kṛpād droṇāc ca saṃyuge tat prāptam adya me yuddhe sūtaputrān mahārathāt
english: What I never met before from Bhīṣma, from Kṛpa, or from Droṇa in combat, that I have met today in battle from the Sūta's son, the great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: tat tvā pṛcchāmi kaunteya yathā hy akuśalas tathā tan mamācakṣva kārtsnyena yathā karṇas tvayā hataḥ
english: Therefore I ask you, son of Kuntī—for I am in distress—tell me in full how Karṇa was slain by you.

sanskrit: śakravīryasamo yuddhe yamatulyaparākramaḥ rāmatulyas tathāstre yaḥ sa kathaṃ vai niṣūditaḥ
english: He whose valor in battle equaled Śakra's, whose might matched Yama's, and who was Rāma's equal in arms—how indeed was he struck down?

sanskrit: mahārathaḥ samākhyātaḥ sarvayuddhaviśāradaḥ dhanurdharāṇāṃ pravaraḥ sarveṣām ekapūruṣaḥ
english: Renowned as a great chariot-warrior, skilled in every kind of fighting, the foremost of bowmen, the one man above all others—

sanskrit: pūjito dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa saputreṇa viśāṃ pate sadā tvadarthaṃ rādheyaḥ sa kathaṃ nihatas tvayā
english: honored by Dhṛtarāṣṭra and his sons, O lord of peoples, ever for your destruction—that son of Rādhā, how was he slain by you?

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭro hi yodheṣu sarveṣv eva sadārjuna tava mṛtyuṃ raṇe karṇaṃ manyate puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: For of all warriors, Arjuna, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that bull among men, ever held Karṇa to be your death in battle.

sanskrit: sa tvayā puruṣavyāghra kathaṃ yuddhe niṣūditaḥ taṃ mamācakṣva bībhatso yathā karṇo hatas tvayā
english: That one, O tiger among men, how was he struck down by you in battle? Tell me, Bībhatsu, how Karṇa was slain by you.

sanskrit: sotsedham asya ca śiraḥ paśyatāṃ suhṛdāṃ hṛtam tvayā puruṣaśārdūla śārdūlena yathā ruroḥ
english: And his lofty head—was it carried off before the eyes of his friends by you, O tiger among men, as a tiger carries off the head of a deer?

sanskrit: yaḥ paryupāsīt pradiśo diśaś ca; tvāṃ sūtaputraḥ samare parīpsan ditsuḥ karṇaḥ samare hastipūgaṃ; sa hīdānīṃ kaṅkapatraiḥ sutīkṣṇaiḥ
english: He, the Sūta's son, who beset every quarter and region, seeking to seize you in battle—Karṇa, who would give away whole droves of elephants in war—is he now, struck by your keen heron-feathered shafts,

sanskrit: tvayā raṇe nihataḥ sūtaputraḥ; kaccic chete bhūmitale durātmā kaccit priyaṃ me paramaṃ tvayādya; kṛtaṃ raṇe sūtaputraṃ nihatya
english: slain by you in battle—does that evil-souled Sūta's son lie upon the earth? Have you done me this day my dearest joy, by slaying the Sūta's son in the fight?

sanskrit: yaḥ sarvataḥ paryapatat tvadarthe; madānvito garvitaḥ sūtaputraḥ sa śūramānī samare sametya; kaccit tvayā nihataḥ saṃyuge 'dya
english: He who ranged on every side for your undoing, drunk with pride and arrogance, that Sūta's son—he who deemed himself a hero—having met him in battle, have you slain him today in combat?

sanskrit: raukmaṃ rathaṃ hastivaraiś ca yuktaṃ; rathaṃ ditsur yaḥ parebhyas tvadarthe sadā raṇe spardhate yaḥ sa pāpaḥ; kaccit tvayā nihatas tāta yuddhe
english: He who, for your undoing, would give away to others a golden chariot yoked with the finest elephants, that wicked one who ever vied in battle—has he been slain by you, my son, in the fight?

sanskrit: yo 'sau nityaṃ śūramadena matto; vikatthate saṃsadi kauravāṇām priyo 'tyarthaṃ tasya suyodhanasya; kaccit sa pāpo nihatas tvayādya
english: He who, ever drunk with the pride of his prowess, would boast in the assembly of the Kauravas, the exceedingly dear friend of Suyodhana—has that wicked one been slain by you today?

sanskrit: kaccit samāgamya dhanuḥpramuktais; tvatpreṣitair lohitārthair vihaṃgaiḥ śete 'dya pāpaḥ sa vibhinnagātraḥ; kaccid bhagno dhārtarāṣṭrasya bāhuḥ
english: Pierced by the blood-seeking birds loosed from your bow and sped by you, does that wicked one lie today with his body cleft? Is the arm of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son broken at last?

sanskrit: yo 'sau sadā ślāghate rājamadhye; duryodhanaṃ harṣayan darpapūrṇaḥ ahaṃ hantā phalgunasyeti mohāt; kaccid dhatas tasya na vai tathā rathaḥ
english: He who, full of arrogance, ever boasted in the midst of kings, gladdening Duryodhana, saying in his folly, 'I am the slayer of Phalguna'—has his chariot now been brought to nothing thereby?

sanskrit: nāhaṃ pādau dhāvayiṣye kadā cid; yāvat sthitaḥ pārtha ity alpabuddhiḥ vrataṃ tasyaitat sarvadā śakrasūno; kaccit tvayā nihataḥ so 'dya karṇaḥ
english: "Never will I wash my feet so long as Pārtha lives"—such was that dull-witted one's vow at all times, O son of Śakra. Has that Karṇa been slain by you this day?

sanskrit: yo 'sau kṛṣṇām abravīd duṣṭabuddhiḥ; karṇaḥ sabhāyāṃ kuruvīramadhye kiṃ pāṇḍavāṃs tvaṃ na jahāsi kṛṣṇe; sudurbalān patitān hīnasattvān
english: He of evil mind who said to Kṛṣṇā, that Karṇa, in the assembly amid the Kuru heroes, 'Why do you not abandon the Pāṇḍavas, Kṛṣṇā—those weaklings, fallen and bereft of strength?'—

sanskrit: yat tat karṇaḥ pratyajānāt tvadarthe; nāhatvāhaṃ saha kṛṣṇena pārtham ihopayāteti sa pāpabuddhiḥ; kaccic chete śarasaṃbhinnagātraḥ
english: That vow which Karṇa made for your undoing—'I shall not come back here without having slain Pārtha together with Kṛṣṇa'—does that evil-minded one now lie with his body riven by arrows?

sanskrit: kaccit saṃgrāme vidito vā tadāyaṃ; samāgamaḥ sṛñjayakauravāṇām yatrāvasthām īdṛśīṃ prāpito 'haṃ; kaccit tvayā so 'dya hataḥ sametya
english: Was this clash of the Sṛñjayas and Kauravas in battle—wherein I was brought to such a plight—made known to him? Has he been slain by you today, joined in combat?

sanskrit: kaccit tvayā tasya sumandabuddher; gāṇḍīvamuktair viśikhair jvaladbhiḥ sakuṇḍalaṃ bhānumad uttamāṅgaṃ; kāyāt prakṛttaṃ yudhi savyasācin
english: Has the head of that exceedingly dull-witted one, with its earrings, radiant as the sun, been severed from its body by you in battle, O Savyasācin, with blazing arrows loosed from the Gāṇḍīva?

sanskrit: yat tan mayā bāṇasamarpitena; dhyāto 'si karṇasya vadhāya vīra tan me tvayā kaccid amogham adya; dhyātaṃ kṛtaṃ karṇanipātanena
english: That for which I, struck down by his arrows, fixed my mind upon you for the slaying of Karṇa, O hero—has that thought of mine been made fruitful by you today through the felling of Karṇa?

sanskrit: yad darpapūrṇaḥ sa suyodhano 'smān; avekṣate karṇasamāśrayeṇa kaccit tvayā so 'dya samāśrayo 'sya; bhagnaḥ parākramya suyodhanasya
english: That with which Suyodhana, full of arrogance, looked down upon us, relying upon Karṇa—has that prop of Suyodhana been broken by you today by your valor?

sanskrit: yo naḥ purā ṣaṇḍhatilān avocat; sabhāmadhye pārthivānāṃ samakṣam sa durmatiḥ kaccid upetya saṃkhye; tvayā hataḥ sūtaputro 'tyamarṣī
english: He who once called us 'barren sesame seeds' in the midst of the assembly, before the eyes of the kings—has that evil-minded, exceedingly wrathful Sūta's son, encountered in battle, been slain by you?

sanskrit: yaḥ sūtaputraḥ prahasan durātmā; purābravīn nirjitāṃ saubalena svayaṃ prasahyānaya yājñasenīm; apīha kaccit sa hatas tvayādya
english: That evil-souled Sūta's son who, laughing, once said, 'She is won by the son of Subala—drag the daughter of Yajñasena here yourself by force!'—has he too been slain by you here this day?
